title: European Parliament committee adopts revised CO2 targets for new vehicles
excerpt: Environment Committee members adopted a proposal adjusting 2035 emissions targets and adding low-carbon steel credits for new cars and vans.
bodyHtml:
The European Parliament reported on November 4, 2026, that Parliament’s Environment Committee adopted its proposal for revised CO2 emissions targets for new cars and vans and incentives for clean vehicles made in the EU. The draft rules were adopted with 48 votes in favour, 30 against and two abstentions.

For passenger cars, members of the European Parliament want to lower the 2035 fleet-wide CO2 emissions reduction target from 100% to 87.5%. Manufacturers would have to compensate for emissions capped at 7.5% of the 2021 EU fleet-wide reference target to reach a target of 95%, by using credits for low-carbon steel made in the EU. For vans, the 2035 target would decrease from 100% to 80%, subject to a 7.5% cap for low-carbon steel credits.

Parliament’s mandate for negotiations with EU governments is expected to be voted during the December 2026 plenary session.
